questions.explain: Four layers: structure (tables/columns/types), relationships (PKs/FKs — the join graph), statistics (row counts, distributions), and data profile (sampled values) — the catalog is a cache, the live database is the source of truth.
options: Only table names
Structure, relationships, statistics, and data profile — catalog is a cache, live DB is the source of truth
Only row counts
Only the execution plans
questions.q: What four layers does automated introspection cover?

questions.explain: Profile per exposed column with TABLESAMPLE (never full scans), recording distinct values (as example_values when ≤20), min/max, and null fraction; new distinct values appearing are a generation-risk signal.
options: Full table scans for every column
Profiling is unnecessary
Profile once and never again
TABLESAMPLE-based profiling capturing distinct values, min/max, null fraction; new values flagged as risk
questions.q: How is data profiling done safely and what does it record?

questions.explain: Diff live introspection against the catalog snapshot: added columns are proposed but never auto-exposed (allowlist is a security boundary); dropped/renamed columns invalidate cached SQL and alert; a DDL trigger keeps an attributed change log.
options: Added columns proposed but never auto-exposed; dropped/renamed invalidate cache and alert; DDL trigger logs changes
Auto-expose everything new
Ignore schema changes
Drop the catalog on any drift
questions.q: How does schema drift detection work and what are the responses?

questions.explain: Nightly sweeps (introspect → upsert → profile → drift report), drift-triggered schema_version bumps and re-embedding, validation-spike-triggered out-of-cycle sweeps, and quarterly human review — catalog never more than 24h from live.
options: Manual updates only
Nightly sweeps plus drift/validation-triggered updates and quarterly review; catalog stays within 24h of live
Weekly full rebuilds only
No automation; DBAs update the catalog
questions.q: What is the self-healing loop's cadence and invariant?

questions.explain: The glossary is a versioned table of business terms (term, definition, canonical SQL fragment, owner) injected into the text-to-SQL prompt; one good definition fixes a whole class of errors and compounds unlike prompt tuning.
options: The glossary is not worth maintaining
A versioned business-term table injected into prompts — the highest-leverage text-to-SQL investment
Hardcode business rules in the application
Let the model infer business meanings
questions.q: Why is glossary management the highest-leverage text-to-SQL investment?

title: Schema Introspection for AI Query Generation
